paragraphs: Azora Software sells short-term rental compliance software to local governments. The problem it targets is that ordinary permitting systems only capture the rentals that volunteer to apply, leaving the rest unseen.

To close that gap the platform aggregates data from more than 75 sources, cross-references listings against property and parcel records, compiles verifiable evidence and connects to a city's code enforcement operations. Permitting then runs against that discovered address list, covering applications, renewals, status tracking and enforcement actions. Separate tools handle transaction reporting and statement reconciliation to support tax auditing and remittance. For enforcement and appeals, the platform generates PDFs and consolidated evidence of rental activity on demand.

Cities are the customer, and other government technology vendors also bring Azora in for short-term rental work beside the platforms those cities already run. The company says it was founded by three experienced professionals with complementary expertise and runs on a lean structure. One of them is a former city manager of Garden City, Utah. The same team previously built STR Helper, which the about page says was acquired by Host Compliance in 2019. Each customer keeps a named project manager who moves from launch into ongoing support.
